text:
liam: Quick nsys question — I'm seeing repeated kernel-selection spikes in the first 10s of a run. It lines up with KV cache cold misses + batching ramp. Any recommended flags to make a clean capture for kernel timeline analysis?
jenna: Can you paste the nsys command you tried? short captures often bias towards warmup noise.
liam: Ran something like `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o out --sample=cpu --duration=12 --force true -- python serve_trace.py` (very rough). Capture size huge and timeline full of short kernels.
own: Two quick things: 1) bracket the window to skip warmup, 2) increase sampling duration to get steady-state. For kernel selection analysis you want the steady region after KV cache warmed + batches stable.
sasha: Agree. I usually do a two-pass: first run a lightweight smoke capture to see warmup time, then bracket a second capture around stable window. Example: run 20-30 iters with `--sample=cpu` off for smoke (small file), then `--capture-range=nvtx:StartStable,StopStable` or `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=timer --start 12 --duration 8` for the stable region.
liam: Hmm we add NVTX markers around the batching ramp already. But NVTX brackets sometimes get truncated when the process forks. Any tips to make sure bracketed markers survive?
jenna: Put NVTX markers in the parent process right before you create worker threads / GPUs. Also use a short pre-warm where you run a couple of prompt requests to populate KV cache and trigger candidate kernel paths. NVTX inlined into the runtime decisions helps correlate kernel selection.
own: On flags: use `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` (you already do) but also try disabling sampling for short runs: `--sample=none` and use `--capture-range=nvtx` to limit file size. For longer steady captures use `--sample=cpu` at 1kHz or 1000 (if available) so you get good temporal resolution without logging every API call.
sasha: Note about sampling bias: very short sample windows (<=5s) bias toward occasional heavy kernels (prefetch, eviction). We found >=8-12s stable window gives representative kernel mix for our batching heuristics.
liam: That matches my intuition. How do you diagnose kernel selection vs kv-evict behavior? Both look like short-lived kernels.
jenna: Use NVTX annotation around KV operations (evict/prefetch) and split the capture into two tracks: one with only KV stress (fire repeated cold requests) and one with real batching. Compare kernel timelines. If kernel names switch when KV ops happen, you can correlate by timestamp. Also look at OSRT timeline to see CPU threads doing prefetch/evict work — sometimes kernel switch is driven by a host-side task that prefers a different cuBLAS/cuDNN kernel.
own: Also check the kernel durations histogram in the nsys report — lots of tiny kernels indicate fragmentation; one-off kernels during eviction may be much longer latency but happen infrequently.
liam: Any practical nsys CLI snippet you'd recommend to reduce noise and file size while keeping useful trace?
sasha: Here's what I've been using:```bash
# smoke run to estimate warmup
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=smoke --sample=none --duration=6 -- python serve_trace.py
# stable bracketed capture (use NVTX markers around stable window)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=stable_capture --sample=cpu --sample-freq=1000 --capture-range=nvtx -- python serve_trace.py
```Replace `--sample-freq` with whatever your nsys supports (some builds use `--sample` options). The key is smoke -> bracketed stable.
jenna: Also gzip the qdrep when sharing and point folks to `nsys-ui` with `nsys-ui stable_capture.qdrep` or generate a timeline CSV: `nsys stats --report=timeline --output=timeline.csv stable_capture.qdrep` for quick grep.
own: Another gotcha: asynchronous prefetch threads can cause kernel hops due to different workspace sizes. If you see alternate kernels (e.g., cudnnTensorOp vs custom fused kernels) align them with NVTX marks for prefetch and with the memory allocator logs.
liam: Good call. Our runtime logs show a KV async prefetch running every 3rd request during cold starts. I’ll add NVTX around that and retake a bracketed capture.
liam: One more Q — when I increase bracket length to 15s, the qdrep ballooned. Any tips to keep capture size manageable?
sasha: - Use `--sample=cpu` instead of event tracing for long windows.
  - Filter CUDA API events if not needed (e.g., skip detailed memory copies with `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` but fine tune cuda-subset if your nsys supports it).
  - Reduce device-side metrics collection (don't request all counters).
  - Post-process with `nsys convert` to extract only timeline slices you need.
nsys-bot: nsys scan complete — created stable_capture.qdrep (220MB) and timeline.csv (4.2MB).
liam: Thanks everyone — I'll run the smoke + bracket workflow, add NVTX for KV prefetch/evict, and share the timeline CSV. If it still looks noisy I'll attach the qdrep (gzipped) and point to a few suspect timestamps. :thumbsup:
